messages.author: eb030f957eb6d9b9
messages.subject: competitions effects and EAR3 models
parts:
Dear breedR users,

I am trying to estimate direct genetic effects (genotypic values), additive and non-additive indirect genetic effects in a dataset where clonal genotypes are spatially arranged in a plot . I would like to simultaneously account for environmental variation and competition in the analysis of my dataset. I read about EAR3 models in the Methods S3 of Costa e Sylva et al 2013. 
My feeling is that the correlation between the residuals of adjacent individuals is constant in an EAR3 model. However, the strengh of the correlation could depend on the difference of genotypic values between adjacent individuals. In other words, the correlation between the residuals of individuals with very different genotypic values would be highly negative (e.g. strong competition due to the shading of the small individual), whereas the correlation between the residuals of individuals with similar genotypic values would be close to zero (i.e. no shading, so no competition).

I was wondering if it would be possible to fit such correlation in breedR or in another program you would know of?
Alternatively, do you know about a tutorial somewhere about how to fit EAR3 models in breedR or in another program?


Thank you very much.

Best regards,

Nicolas

messages.author: 8dbb28b015bb7762
messages.subject: Re: [breedR] competitions effects and EAR3 models
parts:
Dear Nicolas,

The short answer is no: breedR cannot fit these models out of the box.

Most easily, you can account simultaneously for competition and environmental variation with breedR by using the competition genetic model together with the splines spatial effect, for example.

That said, it is possible to do what you want with some work on your side.

1. breedR can perform estimation of direct and indirect additive genetic effects as in Costa e Silva et al. 2013. It corresponds exactly with the [*Competition model*](https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Overview#competition) using a *decay parameter* $\alpha = 1$.

2. You can fit an EAR3 model with breedR, but you have to overcome two limitations:
        2.1 breedR cannot estimate autocorrelation parameters. You need to perform a **grid search**, fixing these parameters at several combinations of values and fitting conditional models. You can then extract the log-likelihood of each of the fitted models with `r logLik(res)` and choose the best combination. EAR3 has two parameters for each dimension, thus a grid search will be computationally costly, but it is mechanical. Consider parallelization.
        2.2. breedR does not know the EAR3 model. But you can easily build the covariance and incidence matrix yourself, and feed them to a [`generic` component](https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Overview#generic-component)

Note, however, that EAR3 is accounting simultaneously for large-scale environmental variation and short-scale competition effects. Thus it is an alternative to the competition model, but I don't think it should be used in combination with it. From my understanding of Costa e Silva et al. 2013, they only use it in the reduced *Model 3*, where there is no explicit account for IGEs.

3. The question of whether there is differential competition depending on whether individuals share genotypes or not is indeed very interesting. It is something we have in our agenda, as well. breedR does not currently support such a competition model, and unfortunately you cannot currently build it yourself, not even using a `generic` component. It will be possible shortly (presumably by July) when I have implemented the possibility of [grouping arbitrary random effects](https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/doc/UI_spec_multitrait.pdf) (see Section 4).


I hope it helps.
